facts.fact: Adwave's article states that people form an initial judgment about a brand in about 90 seconds.
facts.quote: people form an initial judgment in about **90 seconds**

facts.fact: The article cites, via Canva's summary of Institute for Color Research work, that 62% to 90% of the initial assessment can be based on color alone.
facts.quote: the same research body has long been cited to show that **62% to 90%** of that assessment can be based on color alone

facts.fact: The article recommends a 60/30/10 color split with 60% primary, 30% secondary, and 10% accent.
facts.quote: The cleanest brand palettes usually use the **60/30/10 split**, with **60% primary**, **30% secondary**, and **10% accent**

facts.fact: The article recommends keeping a brand palette to three to five colors.
facts.quote: I'd keep it to **three to five colors**.

facts.fact: The article recommends auditing three to five competitors that the audience compares the brand against.
facts.quote: look at the **three to five** businesses your audience compares you against

facts.fact: The article states that in several East Asian contexts white is more closely associated with mourning and funerals, while it often suggests purity in Western markets.
facts.quote: in several East Asian contexts it's more closely associated with mourning and funerals

facts.fact: Adwave states it can place campaigns across more than 100 premium channels.
facts.quote: place campaigns across **100+ premium channels**, and start campaigns at **$30/day** while keeping spend pacing automatic

facts.fact: Adwave states campaigns can start at $30 per day.
facts.quote: start campaigns at **$30/day** while keeping spend pacing automatic

facts.fact: The article recommends running a short brand recall survey within a 24-hour window after the ad airs.
facts.quote: Then run a short recall survey in a **24-hour** window after the spot airs.

facts.fact: The article recommends revisiting the brand color palette on a quarterly cadence as the brand grows.
facts.quote: revisit the palette on a quarterly cadence as the brand grows.
